capabilities: feed-generation | Turns web pages and online services that publish no feed into RSS, Atom, JSON, HTML, MRSS or plain-text feeds, through bridges requested with an HTTP GET.
description:
UnitySVC runs the official RSS-Bridge image in a separate container for each enrollment, with its own HTTPS address. RSS-Bridge is a PHP application that makes feeds for websites that have none. It ships with hundreds of bridges (547 in this version); you open the instance, pick a bridge, fill in its form, and get a feed address in Atom, RSS (MRSS), JSON, HTML or plain text that any feed reader can subscribe to. When a reader asks for the feed, the instance fetches the target site itself and converts what it finds.

Enroll in the base channel and keep or replace the generated sign-in password. The instance is protected by HTTP basic authentication, with the user name and password you set, and every bridge is enabled unless you narrow the list in the enrollment form. Open `https://<instance>/` and sign in, or put the credentials in the feed address (`https://user:password@<instance>/?action=display&bridge=...`) for readers that support it. Nothing is persisted: the instance keeps only a cache that is lost when it stops. See How to use this service for full setup and limitations.

You pay the selected channel's platform compute cost while the instance runs, including idle time. Labs adds no markup and receives no seller payout. See the upstream RSS-Bridge documentation and issue tracker for software-specific help; a bridge can stop working when its target site changes.
